question.text: A company with paid-up capital of Rs.200 crore and free reserves of Rs.600 crore wants to buy back shares. If it passes only a Board resolution (not a special resolution), what is the maximum buyback amount permissible?

explanation.text: The Logic: With only a Board resolution, buyback is limited to 10% of the aggregate of paid-up equity capital and free reserves. Aggregate = Rs.200 cr + Rs.600 cr = Rs.800 cr. 10% of Rs.800 cr = Rs.80 crore. The Trap: Candidates may apply 10% to only paid-up capital (Rs.20 cr) or only to free reserves (Rs.60 cr). The 10% applies to the aggregate of the two. Note: Buyback amounts above the 10% Board-resolution threshold require a special resolution under the applicable framework.
